blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A grid of MILP solves every $500k gives V(10,000) = 812 and V(10,500) = 870 for a capital plan. What can you conclude about the budgets between them?

options.text: V rises in a straight line from 812 to 870 across the gap
options.says: V is a step function: flat stretches and jumps, never a sloped line.

options.text: V steps once, by 58, at some budget strictly inside the gap
options.says: The 116 between two grid points came in four steps; one step is not implied.

options.text: V equals 812 everywhere below 10,500 and jumps there
options.says: The grid cannot place a step; nothing says the jump waits until 10,500.

options.text: V stays from 812 to 870, with steps the solves cannot place
options.says: Right: V never falls as B grows, and a grid only brackets where its steps are.

origin.section: Repeated Solves on a Grid Give Points of the Curve, Not Its Steps

questions.stem: On a curve with whole-$k values, V(B) = 640 at the current budget. The cheapest plan worth at least 641 costs 7,320, and the best plan within 7,320 is worth 655. What is the next step point?

options.text: (7,320, 641), the level the cheapest plan was asked to reach
options.says: The value at a step comes from the second solve, which can pass the level asked for.

options.text: (7,320, 655), the best plan's value at the cheapest plan's cost
options.says: Right: K(641) says where the step is, and V(7,320) says how high.

options.text: (7,319, 655), one unit below the cost of the cheapest plan found
options.says: No plan worth more than 640 fits below 7,320, so V(7,319) is still 640.

options.text: (7,321, 641), one unit above the cost of the cheapest plan found
options.says: The step is at the cheapest plan's cost itself, since V jumps at that budget.

origin.section: The Next Step Is the Cheapest Plan Worth More: Two Solves per Step

questions.stem: A report shows the step point (7,320, 655) and says the best plan there costs 7,280. What follows?

options.text: Nothing: a plan at a step point may cost anything up to its budget
options.says: The best plan at a step costs exactly the step's budget, or the step would be lower.

options.text: The plan is fine, and 40 of the budget at that step goes unused
options.says: A plan worth 655 at 7,280 would put the step at 7,280 or below.

options.text: The step point is wrong, since V would already be 655 at 7,280
options.says: Right: no plan cheaper than a step's budget can be worth as much as the step's value.

options.text: The value is wrong, since a plan costing 7,280 is worth exactly 640
options.says: Nothing fixes a cheaper plan's value at 640; the contradiction is in the step's budget.

origin.section: Each Step Point Is an Efficient Plan of Cost Against Value
